newsitem.title: INDIA: Air-India expects to break even in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Air-India expects to break even in 97/98.

text.p: India's state-owned international carrier Air-India expects to recover from recent losses and break even in 1997/98 (April-March), the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Wednesday.
The news agency said Air-India recorded a profit in January 1997 for the first time in more than 16 months. The airline did not expect to record a profit in the current financial year, it said.

"As per current indications Air-India will achieve an overall net profit in the last quarter of 1996/97. Losses have been coming down every quarter in 1996/97," PTI quoted Air-India managing director Brajesh Kumar as saying.
In 1996/97 the airline registered a nine percent increase in passenger traffic, which had grown by more than 35 percent in the preceding two years, PTI said.
Kumar said the company had invested 35 billion rupees ($974 million) in six new aircraft over the last three years.
During 1995/96 and 1996/97, Air-India had ploughed back more than six billion rupees each year into the company, he said.
